column4: note

enum of the five byte-aligned widths INT32, INT40, INT48, INT56, INT64: bits(), bytes(), mask() (all bits for INT64), minValue/maxValue(signed) (unsigned INT64 maximum is the raw bits -1L), fits/require(value, signed) (ArithmeticException), smallest(value, signed); JDK-only, no state beyond five final fields per constant

signed 48-bit (lint) arithmetic on primitive long values: BITS 48, BYTES 6, MIN/MAX/UNSIGNED_MAX_VALUE, check/checkUnsigned (through M3IntWidth.INT48.require), add/subtract/multiply/divide/negate/absExact (operands and result checked; Math.*Exact catches working-long overflow first), wrap (low 48 bits, sign-extended), saturate; allocates no value object. Its class javadoc keeps the donor sentence that names {@link PackedIntArray#lint(int)} as the six-byte storage: that class is the held donor PackedIntArray (NEC below), so the link does not resolve in jdk.m3.arrays (javac without -Xdoclint does not check it; recorded in GATES.tsv doclint_note)

crate JUnit test, BigInteger as the independent oracle: constants and range checks, 48-bit boundaries of add/subtract, multiply with working-long overflow (1<<40 * 1<<40), divide (zero, MIN / -1), negate/abs at MIN, operand rejection, wrap against BigInteger mod 2^48 over 9 edges + 10,000 seeded longs, saturate, a 6,000-trial seeded campaign of the four exact operations against BigInteger (9 tests)
